text: Routing fixed by the operator for this campaign and every follow-up it spawns: every execution worker is DeepSeek through dsh; every gate judge is gpt-6-astra through codex; GLM 5.3 through zcode reviews; gpt-5.6-luna supervises. Astra is also the reviewing architect of the spec itself and the campaign does not start until it accepts. Note gpt-6-astra is not in the declared catalogue (models prints the gpt-5.6 family) but codex passes model through verbatim and it answers; gpt-6-luna does not exist, luna is gpt-5.6-luna.

Four phases, one per improvement, each independently deliverable and landing on main with the suite, the typecheck and the deterministic evals green at every boundary. Deliberately excluded and recorded as non-goals: the live eval class, evidence-driven routing, golden-set execution, invented model prices, and sandbox work.

Spec fechada com gpt-6-astra em 7 rodadas de revisao adversarial: v1 REJECT/10 issues, v2 REJECT/10 resolvidos+3 novos, v3 REJECT/3 issues, v4 REJECT/1 issue central errado (normalizeProviderResult nao e choke point unico de custo), v5 REJECT/4 gaps na enumeracao de call sites, v6 REJECT/1 gap (recordInvocationUsage nao persistia os campos que calculava), v7 ACCEPT. Cada rodada foi verificada contra o codigo real antes da proxima versao. Spec final copiada para docs/ desta campanha.

Phase 1 delivered to main at 8163fd7: deferred reads accepted when a transitive dependency's writeFiles/writeRoots covers the path, all 9 named done-when cases as tests, packetHash equality proven, worker-result.mjs stays strict. First-pass gate approval by astra, no revisions, no scope findings. Suite 673/673, typecheck clean, evals 17/17. dsh-deepseek worker, codex-astra judge (glm fallback unused, astra stayed available throughout).

Phase 2 delivered to main at 4f50a9b (after 810263f): resume --answer <node>=<path>, split 2a/2b. Both nodes needed one revision each: 2a's astra gate caught a real edge case (--answer + --node combined silently mis-scoped a dependant), fixed by refusing the combination outright; 2b's gate caught a finalVerification failure the contract itself was scoped wrong for (source-shape.test.mjs not writable), fixed within existing scope. After integration, full npm test caught a gap my own Phase 2 contract left: finalVerification never covered test/docs/, so the new documentation silently overflowed the byte ceiling Phase 1 had already raised once. Fixed directly (trim + second justified raise), not worth a worker node. Suite 681/681, typecheck clean, evals 17/17.

Phase 3 delivered to main at 0b5c622: next command in src/report/next.mjs, six ranked predicates, --json, wired into cli.mjs. First-pass gate: astra found a real edge case at minor severity (below the major/critical failOn, so it integrated without a revision): rank 5 declares every linked run terminal by absence of any node candidate/in-progress signal, which is vacuously true for a linked run with zero node snapshots (a controller dead at bootstrap, or a linked run id whose directory does not exist) -- next would wrongly report the campaign closable. Deliberately not fixed now: minor, non-blocking, narrow (bootstrap-crash-before-first-write only), and fixing it mid-campaign would cost a revision cycle for a correctness gap that does not affect any delivered phase. Left for the end-of-campaign retrospective and its own follow-up campaign. Suite 693/693, typecheck clean, evals 17/17.

next.mjs rank 5 (all linked runs terminal) needs a real per-run terminality proof -- a linked run directory with no node snapshots at all must surface at rank 4 (unknowable/non-terminal), mirroring how a torn snapshot is handled, not be counted as terminal by omission. Evidence: astra's minor finding on next-command (operator-loop-phase3-20260913), next.mjs:108-141 and :328-330. Deferred to the end-of-campaign retrospective.

Roteamento alterado a pedido do operador: conta DeepSeek ficou sem saldo (Insufficient Balance) durante cost-propagation, worker sem fallback declarado, nó esgotou. Operador pediu: workers passam a usar GLM. Aplicado para o restante da campanha: novo runtime zcode-glm-worker (zcode, glm-5.3, permissionMode yolo, escrita habilitada -- o zcode-glm-judge existente era plan/leitura, nao serviria como worker). Removido o fallback do juiz codex-astra para zcode-glm-judge, que agora compartilharia vendor (zhipu) com o worker e seria recusado em tempo de execucao como judge_fallback_vendor_conflict. Astra fica sem fallback: se esgotar de novo, o no para e isso e reportado diretamente, nao degradado silenciosamente.

Operador pediu resiliencia total do worker: deepseek-flash, glm-5.3-flash, gpt-5.6-luna, gemini-3.8-flash-low, cliclando pelo primeiro que liberar cota, campanha nunca deve parar exceto se todos esgotarem. Verificado no codigo (src/engine/backoff.mjs planRoute): .fallback e' um salto unico, nunca cadeia ('one hop, never a chain over every other runtime'), mas existe um mecanismo diferente e ja construido -- composedWorker/nextSameTierRuntime -- que percorre TODOS os runtimes do mesmo tier automaticamente a cada esgotamento, sem limite de saltos, e so bloqueia (runtime_tier_exhausted, status blocked) quando todos exaurem. Ativado omitindo runtimeDefaults.worker e node.runtime (src/engine/assignment.mjs:37). Usado para esta correcao. gpt-5.6-luna EXCLUIDO do pool: e' codex/openai, mesmo vendor do juiz fixo codex-astra; a checagem de vendor-conflito e' estatica e so roda quando o worker e' pinado (contract/index.mjs), entao um worker composto nunca e' checado contra o vendor do juiz -- se o roteamento dinamico caisse em luna, astra estaria julgando o proprio vendor sem deteccao. Pool final: dsh-deepseek-flash, zcode-glm-flash, agy-gemini-flash, todos tier 1, judge fixo codex-astra sem fallback.

Pedido do operador, nao implementado hoje: quando TODOS os runtimes de um tier esgotam (blocked/runtime_tier_exhausted), o sistema hoje fica bloqueado ate um operador rodar resume manualmente. O pedido e' que o sistema analise deterministicamente qual runtime esgotado libera primeiro (cada erro ja carrega exhaustedUntil) e continue sozinho quando esse instante chegar, sem intervencao humana -- 'a campanha nunca deve parar'. Isso e' capacidade nova: nem o supervise mecanico (so reinicia controlador morto) nem o retry planner (planResumeRetry classifica runtime_tier_exhausted como hold, exige decisao explicita) fazem isso hoje. Candidato a fase 5 / campanha de follow-up com o mesmo Astra-review, mesma config de agentes.

Astra encontrou (severidade minor, abaixo do failOn, integrou sem bloquear): dois tipos de registro de costUsd que o pacote da fase 4 nunca nomeou explicitamente ficaram sem costProvenance pareado. (1) engine/lifecycle.mjs:523-525 -- buildRouting recebe costUsd: envelope.costUsd para o routing.history (trilha de auditoria do roteamento, nao o costProjection); (2) engine/bulk-read.mjs -- a propria funcao publica bulkRead() (nao accountDelegation, que foi corrigido) retorna costUsd: envelope.costUsd ?? null em dois lugares (sucesso e falha) sem provenance, e BulkReadResult nem declara o campo. Nenhum dos dois alimenta usage.jsonl ou os dois consumidores de metricas -- e' por isso que a severidade ficou minor. Candidato a limpeza na campanha de follow-up.

Phase 4 delivered to main at 1e484de: priceUsage puro, runtimes[].pricing no schema, costProvenance no invocation allowlist, wiring nos dois pontos de origem reais (recordInvocationUsage, invocationResult) e em todos os sites derivados nomeados na spec (recover.mjs, lifecycle.mjs, bulk-read.mjs), consumidores de metricas atualizados. cost-core: 1a tentativa, pass, julgado por GLM (fallback do Astra ativo na epoca). cost-propagation: precisou de 3 runs distintas por 3 motivos diferentes -- (1) erro meu de escopo (process.mjs faltando em writeFiles, corrigido), (2) DeepSeek sem saldo, GLM no limite de 5h, exigiu trocar workers para pool de tier composto (deepseek-flash/glm-5.3-flash/gemini-3.8-flash-low, sem fallback de fallback -- .fallback e' um salto unico, verificado no codigo), (3) worker DeepSeek-flash travou (stall_timeout) duas vezes durante verificacao longa na mesma run, sem relacao com cota. Ao todo 4 tentativas nessa run final: 2 stalls, 1 rejeicao real do gate (arquivo de producao passou de 800 linhas, corrigido dentro do escopo), 1 aprovacao com achado minor (dois tipos de registro de custo fora do escopo nomeado, ja registrados como open-question). Campanha inteira: 4 fases, main em 1e484de, suite 708/708, typecheck limpo, evals 17/17.

All four phases delivered to main (8163fd7, 4f50a9b, 0b5c622, 1e484de). Spec dialogue with astra: 7 review rounds, every rejection pointed at a real, verifiable defect in the proposed design (missing recovery-path call sites, an override schema that would fail validation, a rank overlap) -- the process worked exactly as intended and each round's cost was justified by what it caught. Execution: 3 of 4 phases passed first-pass gate; phase 2 needed one real fix (an --answer/--node combination left a dependant mis-scoped) and one contract-authoring gap of my own (finalVerification never covered test/docs/, caught only by running the full suite myself before push -- the same class of gap recurred in phase 4's writeFiles). Phase 3 and phase 4 each closed with a minor, non-blocking finding astra caught and this session deliberately deferred rather than spending another live cycle on: next.mjs's rank 5 treats a linked run with zero node snapshots as vacuously terminal; phase 4 left two record shapes (routing.history, bulkRead's own return value) without paired costProvenance. Both are real and narrow. Routing held for phases 1-3 (deepseek-v4-pro worker, astra judge, glm mechanical fallback, never triggered) and broke down in phase 4 under real resource exhaustion: DeepSeek balance ran out, then astra's own openai quota, then GLM's 5-hour window, then DeepSeek-flash stalled twice mid-verification. The operator's fix -- a same-tier composed worker pool across three vendors instead of a single pinned runtime, discovered by reading src/engine/backoff.mjs's planRoute directly since contract.md's own wording ('one hop, never a chain') undersold what nextSameTierRuntime already does -- worked, and surfaced the standing ask this retrospective forwards: exhausting an entire tier still only blocks the node for a human to notice, it does not wait for the earliest recorded exhaustedUntil and continue on its own. That gap, plus the two minor findings above, are the concrete backlog for a follow-up campaign under the same agent con…
